title: API Gateways, Load Balancing & Reverse Proxies (PYTH_162_S1 to PYTH_162_S8)

slides.title: API Gateway Patterns
slides.prompt: API Gateways sit between clients and backend microservices, providing routing, rate limiting, and SSL termination.

slides.title: Reverse Proxy Routing
slides.prompt: Fill in the Nginx directive used to pass incoming HTTP requests to a backend Python server.

slides.title: Load Balancing Algorithms
slides.prompt: Which load balancing algorithm distributes requests sequentially across all available healthy backend nodes?

slides.title: SSL/TLS Offloading
slides.prompt: Fill in the protocol term for terminating HTTPS encrypted traffic at the gateway before routing plain HTTP internally.

slides.title: Gateway Rate Limiting
slides.prompt: Why is rate limiting best enforced at the API Gateway level instead of individual Python worker nodes?
options: It drops excessive malicious traffic before it reaches expensive Python application compute layers
It forces clients to clear local browser cookies
It speeds up database write operations
It prevents Docker container images from expiring
slides.correctAnswer: It drops excessive malicious traffic before it reaches expensive Python application compute layers

slides.title: HTTP Forwarded Headers
slides.prompt: Fill in the HTTP header used by proxies to preserve the client's original IP address.

slides.title: Circuit Breaker at Gateway
slides.prompt: What primary protection does an API Gateway circuit breaker offer during downstream microservice outages?
options: It fails fast with an instant fallback error, avoiding cascading timeout queues
It reboots the physical cloud server host
It automatically deletes corrupt database rows
It converts all POST requests into GET requests
slides.correctAnswer: It fails fast with an instant fallback error, avoiding cascading timeout queues

slides.title: Traefik / Nginx API Gateway
slides.prompt: Fill in the modern cloud-native reverse proxy popular in Kubernetes environments.
